I don't test software to prove it works — I test it to find where it won't. 🔍

Nearly 3 years across government, banking, SaaS and AI platforms have taught me the interesting bugs never sit on the happy path. I go looking for the gap between what was built, what was asked for, and what a real user actually does — and I don't stop until I've found it. That instinct is what separates testing from actually protecting a release. 🕵️

🐨 Digital Fundraising Platform — Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary

Project Manager & QA Lead · Jul–Dec 2025 · Gold Coast

Topic

Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary needed a release-ready digital fundraising platform within a fixed timeline, with critical donation, payment and user workflows thoroughly tested before stakeholder sign-off.

My contribution
  • Took dual ownership of QA and project coordination, connecting testing priorities directly with delivery risk.
  • Planned and executed Functional, Integration, Regression, E2E and UAT testing across the platform.
  • Used Postman and SQL to validate APIs, integrations and backend data.
  • Managed the end-to-end defect lifecycle in Jira, collaborating with developers and stakeholders to prioritise issues, validate fixes and assess release readiness.
  • Redesigned the Jira QA dashboard — bringing defect severity, status, ownership and testing progress into one clear view — after noticing defect reporting was creating unnecessary back-and-forth.
Conclusion

The platform reached release readiness within the planned timeline, with critical workflows validated for stakeholder sign-off. The improved Jira reporting approach contributed to an estimated 20% improvement in testing and reporting efficiency, reducing manual status chasing and giving the team clearer visibility of release risk.

Skills gained
QA & project leadershipJira dashboard designDefect traceabilityFunctional / Integration / Regression / E2E / UAT testingAPI & data validation (Postman, SQL)Stakeholder coordination

🛡️ Web Security Risk Management — RocketReach

Risk & Compliance Lead · Academic Project · Griffith University

Risk Assessment · ISO 31000 · NIST SP 800-30 · Incident Response · JIRA

Topic

RocketReach, a web platform client for this project, faced a range of web-based cyber threats — clickjacking, formjacking, QR code phishing (quishing) and typosquatting — with no structured way to identify, prioritise or respond to risk across its digital environment.

My contribution
  • Built a Risk and Control Matrix (RCM) linking each identified risk to preventative and detective controls.
  • Rated and prioritised risks using a 5x5 likelihood/impact matrix, aligned to NIST SP 800-30 and ISO 31000.
  • Designed the quarterly risk management plan and the incident response plan — detection, response, containment, recovery and lessons learned — each mapped to a Gantt timeline.
  • Defined the stakeholder engagement and communication plan, including JIRA-tracked risk items and escalation paths.
Conclusion

Delivered a complete, standards-aligned risk management and incident response framework for RocketReach as part of a four-person postgraduate project team, covering risk identification through to continual improvement.

Skills gained
Risk & Control Matrix designISO 31000 / NIST SP 800-30Incident response planningStakeholder communication planning
